source: The frequency of famine years by region (W30): famine years per thousand farmed years, judged at the end of the dev W5 solve arm (YD to 1 CE) over the land cells inside each region's box [lonMin, lonMax, latMin, latMax] that farmers stood on (farmedYears > 0). A famine year is the label 04 §4.2 defines (a bottom-decile anomaly whose harvest fails by more than a third); the windows are the pre-modern historical famine chronologies named per region, set before the first measurement and never widened to pass. The boxes are the yield-variance table's.
statistic: pooled sum of famineYears over the sum of farmedYears, per thousand, over the box's land cells with farmedYears > 0

regions.name: England and northern France
regions.source: Campbell and Ó Gráda 2011 (Harvest shortfalls, grain prices, and famines in preindustrial England, JEH): national harvests a third or more short in 1315-16, 1321, 1438, 1555-56 and 1596-97, seven years in three centuries; Hoskins 1964/1968 (harvest fluctuations 1480-1759). A famine year one in thirty to three hundred; v1's ~2 per millennium was its own output (research/03), not a datum

regions.name: Greece and the Aegean
regions.source: Gallant 1991 (Risk and Survival in Ancient Greece: a wheat crop failing about one year in four on the dry margin, barley one in twenty); Garnsey 1988 (Famine and Food Supply in the Graeco-Roman World: food crises frequent, famines with mortality rarer). A famine year one in seven to thirty

regions.name: The Sahel
regions.source: Cissoko 1968 (famines and epidemics at Timbuktu and the Niger bend, 16th-18th c.); Watts 1983 (Silent Violence: chronic famine in Hausaland); the recorded 20th-century Sahel famines 1913-14, 1931, 1942, 1968-74 and 1983-85, thirteen years in a century. A famine year one in five to twenty

regions.name: The Nile valley
regions.source: Hassan 1981 (the Roda nilometer floods, low floods one year in five to ten, the failed flood rarer); Allouche 1994 (al-Maqrizi's Ighathat al-umma, the Egyptian famine chronology); Ó Gráda 2009 (Famine: A Short History, the Egyptian series). A famine year one in twelve to fifty

regions.name: The Deccan interior
regions.source: Famine Commission 1880 (the Deccan famine chronology from 1396); Bhatia 1967 (Famines in India: the interior's major famines about one in twenty to fifty years, lesser scarcities more often). A famine year one in ten to fifty

regions.name: The North China Plain
regions.source: Deng Yunte 1937 (History of Famine Relief in China: a drought or flood famine on the plain most decades); Yao 1942 (the flood and drought chronology 206 BCE-1911); Will 1990 (Bureaucracy and Famine in Eighteenth-Century China). A famine year one in seven to twenty-five
